title.narrative: Support to Sustainable Reintegration of Returnees, IDPs and Vulnerable Host Communities in Afghanistan 2021

description.narrative: The proposed project aims at improving livelihoods, health and life quality on a sustainable basis for returnees, protracted IDPs and their vulnerable host communities. By the completion of the project, beneficiaries would have improved livelihoods as measured by reduced time in collecting water and increased time spent on food production, income generation and girls’ and boys’ education, improved health as measured by a reduction in water borne diseases, and an overall improvement in the quality of life as perceived by the targeted men, women, boys and girls. The integrated nature and the diverse targeting strategy of the interventions will enable addressing of the needs and priorities of the communities from different angles; access to and use of safe drinking water coupled with open defecation free villages and improved hygiene behavior will reduce the incidence of diseases (including COVID19) which will in turn enable communities to invest increased time, energy and resources into learning new skills and engaging in various farm and off farm income generating activities offered by the intervention. The interventions planned will particularly target at risk individuals and households such as women-headed households, youth susceptible to embracing negative coping mechanisms, impoverished farmers and individuals with disability. Based on learning since outbreak of Covid-19 in March 2020the interventions for this extension period will also focus on helping communities to reduce the negative economic impact of COVID19 pandemic.

title.narrative: 6. (Women’s Empowerment): Vulnerable women from among the returnees, IDPs and their host communities have access to social, and economic resources, and capacity to empower women

1. % of women-headed households who have achieved improved food security. Target: 80% of 180 2. % of women with improved literacy. Target: 90% of 200 3. # of women headed families who suffer from food shortages have achieved temporary food security. Target: 3000 families (21,000 individuals)

target.value: 1. % of women-headed households who have achieved improved food security. Target: 80% of 180 2. % of women with improved literacy. Target: 90% of 200 3. # of women headed families who suffer from food shortages have achieved temporary food security. Target: 3000 families (21,000 individuals)

actual.value: 1. 97% of survey participants have achieved improved food security. Out of which 83% of the survey participants shows that they are able to sufficiently feed their families and cover the expenses related to their basic needs. 2. 85% of the interviewed beneficiaries confirmed that they can read, write and do basic calculations after their graduation from DACAAR’s literacy programme. 3. 4,000 women-headed families (approximately 28,000 individuals) (51%women) have received Food Security Package (100 kg of Wheat flour, 7kg of beans, 7 kg of Liquid Oil and 1 kg of salt) for vulnerable host community, IDP and returnee beneficiaries.

6.2 Most vulnerable women headed households provided with food security packages and home based farming, and food processing training and support

-#of food security packages distributed and # of households targeted
#of home-based farms established

target.value:
-#of food security packages distributed and # of households targeted Target: 100 packages for same number of HHs
#of home-based farms established Target: 40

actual.value: • 100 women-headed household received food security packages: 99 of them received 2 dairy goats, while one beneficiary received 3 cockerels, 27 hens, and 3 feeder and drinker poultry medication. • 40 women received training and inputs for home-based poultry management. Each one of them received: 10 hens, 2 roosters, 100 kg feed, 1 feeders and drinker, and poultry medication. • 40 women received training and inputs for food processing, in two centres. The topics covered by the training: safe food handling; proper hygiene; marketing; labelling and packaging. The first centre produces jam, pickle and ketchup, while the second, focuses on cake and cookies baking.
